title: Devices & I/O multiplexing
subsystem_derivation: 03 §4.4 (devices — governing capability). LAW = device registration as amendments (capability is law); DECISIONS = bind / unbind / grant; INPUTS = interrupts and completions as arrival events; CACHE = the live binding table; STREAM = I/O throughput aggregates.

rows.what_it_does: Device- or fs-specific control: query ops (read state, capabilities).
rows.conformance_note: Query ioctls (read state, capabilities) = CACHE-only read. The op number determines the class. [Sub-row of design/10 §7's mixed ioctl row, split exactly where that row's own note splits it.]
rows.probe_absent_reason: the devices group is inactive until EP-29 (design/36 §6). A row's probe steps are row DATA in this same file; they are authored when the group activates, so activation is a data change in this tree and never a harness-code change.

rows.what_it_does: Device- or fs-specific control: command ops (configure, bind, reset, submit).
rows.conformance_note: Command ioctls (configure, bind, reset, submit) = DECISION crossing the typed driver envelope (§4.4) — recorded, cites the device's capability rule. Terminal TCGET/SET, block BLK*, etc. Per-driver errno (ENOTTY/EINVAL) identical.
rows.probe_absent_reason: the devices group is inactive until EP-29 (design/36 §6). A row's probe steps are row DATA in this same file; they are authored when the group activates, so activation is a data change in this tree and never a harness-code change.

rows.conformance_note: I/O throughput is STREAM (§4.4); the payload delivered to/from userland is full-fidelity. The device bind (open/ioctl) was the recorded DECISION. Blocking/O_NONBLOCK/EAGAIN semantics identical.
rows.probe_absent_reason: the devices group is inactive until EP-29 (design/36 §6). A row's probe steps are row DATA in this same file; they are authored when the group activates, so activation is a data change in this tree and never a harness-code change.

rows.conformance_note: INPUT (readiness arrivals) + block/wake DECISION. Level/edge-trigger (EPOLLET), timeout, EINTR semantics identical.
